To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
CD40L is not required for CD8+ T-cell priming against a secreted Ag expressed by L. monocytogens and that cross-priming can occur in the presence of CD40L blockade.
CD40L- CD40 interactions are not required for CD8+ T priming against exogenously expressed model Ags during infection with L. monocygenes.
L. monocytogenesis infection overcomes the requirement for CD40 ligand in exogenous Ag presentation to CD8+ cells.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new strategies for vaccination against bacterial infections.
the mechanisms by which the immune system can be stimulated to respond to exogenously presented Ags.
the mechanisms of immune response and tolerance induction to infectious pathogens and their components.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
CD40L- CD40 interactions are not required for CD8+ T-cell priming against nonsecreted bacterial antigens during infection.
L. monocytugenesis infection can overcome CD40 ligand requirement for exogenous Ag presentation to CD8+ cells.
L. monocytogenses is able to overcome the need for CD40 ligand in CD8+T cell cross priming.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
CD40L- CD40 interactions are dispensable for the induction of CD8+ CTLs against nonsecreted bacterial antigens, even though they are essential for the priming of CD4+ T lymphocytes.
L. monocytogene infection can overcome the requirement for CD40 ligand in exogenous Ag presentation to CD8+T cells.
CD40L- CD40 interactions are required for the priming of CD4+ T helper responses to exogenous Ags, but are dispensable for priming CD8+ T helper responses.
The main takeaway from our work is that
during bacterial infection, the requirement for CD40L in the cross-priming process is overcome.
the immune response to a nonsecreted bacterial protein does not require CD40/CD40L interactions.
the requirement for CD40L in CD8 T cell priming is overcome in the context of a bacterial infection.
